entries.title: DEEP/ULTRA brief states another company's news as the target's own facts: the structured news leg feeds the unfiltered region-wide feed blend to synthesis with no relevance gate (BDL brief claimed Sterling and Wilson's Rs 985 cr order and solar/storage projects)
entries.repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Bharat Dynamics - order book, margins and valuation' --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini --autonomy auto, research_depth=deep, symbol=BDL -> published brief: 'BDL has secured ... contracts exceeding Rs 985 crore ... [8]' and '534.3 MWp solar project ... 616 MWh energy storage' cited to [8] 'News for BDL' (vysted://news/BDL); the news tool result item 1e4af0a955903e90 is 'Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy shares rally 8% after securing Rs 985 crore ... orders', symbols: [].
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/12-deep-bdl-4omini.jsonl, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/21-news-tool-BDL.json; sidecar/services/research/deep.py:376-393, deep.py:715-716, deep.py:1140-1148 (news dim folded as one generic source, no per-item check); contrast sidecar/services/research/fast.py:455-498 (_news_value gates the same blend via relevance.row_relevant, R13 ledger #9); sidecar/services/news_provider.py:63-98 (region-wide feeds folded in unlabelled). Refuter: admitted, critical.
entries.root_cause: _record_structured folds the whole news tool result (129 items, most symbols: [] market-wide noise) into one 'News for <SYM>' source; the R13 #9 off-entity gate was added only to fast._news_value and never ported to the DEEP/ULTRA structured news leg.
entries.fix_shape: Route the DEEP/ULTRA structured news leg through the same relevance.row_relevant filter fast._news_value uses (share one helper, don't copy), drop off-entity items with the honest no-on-entity-news note, and cite each kept item as its own source. Pin with a test feeding a blended news result (one on-entity, one off-entity symbols:[] item) through the deep structured path and asserting the off-entity item never reaches the researcher context.

entries.title: ULTRA cross-check prints AGREE (and hides the reason) for claims the verifier reported UNVERIFIED, because _parse_verdict substring-scans the whole line instead of reading the leading verdict word
entries.repro: python -c "from services.research.verify import _parse_verdict; print(_parse_verdict('UNVERIFIED - no source confirms the 23% operating margin.'))" -> ('agree', ...); also 'UNVERIFIED - evidence does not support the figure' and 'UNVERIFIED - no matching figure' -> agree. The ULTRA brief renders '- **AGREE** - <claim>' with detail suppressed.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/research/verify.py:102-116, verify.py:199-207, verify.py:268, verify.py:273, verify.py:396; sidecar/tests/test_research_verify.py:191-197 (only covers 'cannot tell'). Refuter: admitted, critical (reproduced exactly).
entries.root_cause: The prompt mandates a leading <VERDICT> token but the parser checks agree/disagree marker substrings across the whole first line; reasons for UNVERIFIED routinely contain 'confirm'/'support'/'match'.
entries.fix_shape: Parse the first word (strip '*:-'), exact-match UNVERIFIED/DISAGREE/AGREE, fall back to marker scan only when the head is not a verdict token; add the three proven UNVERIFIED strings to test_parse_verdict. Apply the same first-token convention to deep._reflect_says_complete (see R15-RESEARCH-034 (COD-research-depth-iter-deep-13)).

entries.title: DEEP/ULTRA brief [n] citations point at unrelated documents: markers minted against one round's source numbering survive into a brief published under a re-ranked, longer list (price/P&E chips open 'Change in Directorate' PDFs)
entries.repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Deep research on Blue Star (BLUESTARCO): ... Cite sources.' --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini --autonomy auto, research_depth=deep -> brief cites 'Closing Price Rs 1,525.0 [6]', 'P/E 61.67 [7]'; rail [7] = nsearchives BLUESTARCO ... change in directors PDF, [6] = Q1FY27 shareholder communication; figures actually came from [11] vysted://price / [12] vysted://fundamentals. Same on ULTRA HAL (13-ultra-hal-4omini.jsonl); absent on the control run whose list never changed (12-deep-bdl-4omini.jsonl).
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r4-deep-bluestar-4omini.jsonl, replay-r4-deep-bluestar-4omini.json, 13-ultra-hal-4omini.jsonl, 12-deep-bdl-4omini.jsonl, EVIDENCE.md 'Finding 1'; sidecar/services/research/deep.py:356-373 (all_sources ranks web/filings ahead of structured), sidecar/services/research/iter.py:127-129 (_numbered_sources renumbers every round), iter.py:223-260 (synthesis reuses working-report markers). Refuter: admitted, high (transcript proves the mismatch; line-level mechanism corroborated, not traced statement-by-statement).
entries.root_cause: Source numbering is recomputed from a re-ranked, growing list each round while the evolving report text keeps markers minted under the earlier numbering; citecheck only strips out-of-range markers, so in-range stale ones ship.
entries.fix_shape: Give every source a stable id at first sight (append-only numbering; rank only for display/priority, never renumber after a marker exists), or rewrite report markers by URL whenever the list is re-ranked. Pin with a multi-round iter test where round 2 inserts sources ahead of round 1's and the final brief's [n] still resolves to the round-1 URL.

entries.title: ULTRA cross-check mangles every figure that starts a claim line ('40.5%' -> '5%', '-0.4%' -> '4%', '67.13953' -> '13953') and its step reports 'verified 5 numeric claim(s), 0 disagreement(s)' over five UNVERIFIED rows
entries.repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Research Kaynes Technology in depth: ...' --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --autonomy auto, research_depth=ultra -> body: revenue growth +40.5%, P/E 67.13953; '## Cross-check' renders 'UNVERIFIED - 5%', 'UNVERIFIED - 4%', 'UNVERIFIED - 13953'; trace: 'cross-check: verified 5 numeric claim(s), 0 disagreement(s)'. Same on gpt-4o-mini HAL ('P/E 34.42' -> '42', 'Gross Margin 51.70%' -> '70%').
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r3-ultra-kaynes.jsonl + .stdout.txt, replay-r3-ultra-kaynes.json, 13-ultra-hal-4omini.jsonl; sidecar/services/research/verify.py:137-158 (_extract_claims routes claims through _split_subquestions), sidecar/services/research/deep.py:179-202 (strips leading '<digits>.'/'-' with no following-space requirement), verify.py:412-418 (label counts checks, not verified). Refuter: admitted, high (reproduced in-process).
entries.root_cause: Claim extraction reuses the sub-question splitter, whose ordered-list/bullet stripping eats the integer part of a leading decimal and a leading minus sign; the step label interpolates len(checks).
entries.fix_shape: Give claims their own splitter that strips '<digits>. ' only when followed by whitespace + non-digit and never strips a sign; make the step label state verified/unverified/disagree counts separately. Pin with a test over '40.5% revenue growth', '-0.4% earnings growth', '67.13953 P/E' asserting the extracted claim text is unchanged.

entries.title: On the local (zero-setup) lane DEEP/ULTRA synthesis hits the 60 s per-call cap and silently ships the structured floor, labelled 'web coverage for this name is thin' while 13+ web sources were captured, with raw floats and no degraded_reason
entries.repro: vy.py invoke copilot 'Do a deep research brief on CG Power ... order book, margins, valuation vs peers' --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --autonomy auto, research_depth=deep -> step 'synthesize | wrote brief from evolving report | 60014 ms'; published markdown = '_Web coverage for this name is thin; ..._' + filings list + 'change % -1.527472527472525' + 'market cap 1411777036288.0' while the brief carries 13 http web sources; panel header 'DEEP - 21 sources', no note, execution.degraded_reason null. Also 11-deep-bdl-llama (60007 ms) and r3-ultra-kaynes (all three angle syntheses 60001-60012 ms).
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/r2-deep-cgpower.jsonl + .stdout.txt, 11-deep-bdl-llama.jsonl, r3-ultra-kaynes.stdout.txt, replay-r2-deep-cgpower.json; sidecar/services/research/deep.py:165 (_LLM_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECS=60.0), deep.py:173 (_safe_llm -> '' on timeout), sidecar/services/research/iter.py:260-272 (empty synthesis + empty report -> floor), deep.py:459-505 (raw f'{label} {val}'), deep.py:523-556 (floor copy). Refuter: admitted, high.
entries.root_cause: A fixed 60 s per-LLM-call cap sized for hosted models degrades every local-lane distill/synthesis to empty; the floor fallback hardcodes a 'thin web coverage' explanation regardless of why it fired and records no degraded reason.
entries.fix_shape: Scale the per-call cap by provider class (local vs hosted) or stream synthesis against a progress deadline; when the floor fires because synthesis returned empty, set execution.degraded_reason='synthesis_timeout' and a brief.note naming it; only claim thin coverage when web sources are actually empty; format floor numbers through the percent/INR-crore formatters. Pin with a test where the LLM stub times out and web sources exist, asserting degraded_reason and the absence of the thin-coverage copy.

entries.title: ULTRA cross-check runs unmetered after its entry check: up to 1 extract + 5 sequential 60 s verdict calls inside a '90 s' BudgetGuard, which can push the whole ULTRA brief past the runtime dispatch guard and lose it as a timeout
entries.repro: ULTRA run whose 5 extracted claims each take a slow verdict turn: cross_check() calls budget.breach() once at entry, then extract + parallel searches/native calls + a SEQUENTIAL loop of up to 5 _verdict_for calls each capped only at 60 s by _safe_llm -> ~360 s inside BudgetGuard(max_wall_seconds=90); only bound is the agent-runtime research dispatch guard (570 s for ULTRA), whose breach discards the whole brief.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/research/verify.py:37-41 (docstring claims 'SAME BudgetGuard' - false), verify.py:304, verify.py:319, verify.py:357-394, sidecar/services/research/deep.py:165, sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:78, deep_research.py:231-236, deep_research.py:272 (fresh guard); sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:579-615,652-667 (refuter context). Refuter: admitted, high.
entries.root_cause: The cross-check round builds its own BudgetGuard and checks it once; the per-claim loop has no breach re-check and no asyncio.timeout.
entries.fix_shape: Wrap the claim loop in asyncio.timeout(budget.max_wall_seconds) and re-check budget.breach() before each _verdict_for, degrading the remaining claims to UNVERIFIED with the existing out-of-budget reason; fix the docstring. Pin with a test whose verdict stub sleeps past the budget and asserts the round returns within budget with the tail marked UNVERIFIED.

entries.title: Any URL with '/investor' in its path or an 'ir.' host is ranked PRIMARY (exchange/regulator grade), so a Medium or WordPress post outranks Reuters, owns marker [1], and the synthesis prompt tells the model [1] is the primary record
entries.repro: sidecar/.venv/bin/python: domain_tier('https://medium.com/investor-diary/why-i-bought-xyz') -> 1 (TIER_PRIMARY); domain_tier('https://someblog.wordpress.com/ir/2024/hot-tip') -> 1; domain_tier('https://reuters.com/markets/x') -> 2; rank_sources([Reuters, Medium]) -> ['Blog','Reuters']; priority_note -> 'primary record (exchange/regulator/filings/IR): [1]'.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/research/finance.py:72, finance.py:127-132, finance.py:140, finance.py:173; sidecar/services/research/deep.py:368, sidecar/services/research/iter.py:845. Refuter: admitted, high (reproduced; also '/markets/investors-rush' news paths).
entries.root_cause: _looks_like_ir is a substring/prefix heuristic ('/investor' anywhere in the path, any 'ir.' host) guarding the table that decides source authority.
entries.fix_shape: Require a corroborated IR signal (ir./investors. host prefix AND host not on a publishing-platform denylist - medium.com, *.wordpress.com, substack.com, seekingalpha.com, reddit.com) or give IR its own tier between PRIMARY and PRESS. Pin with a table test of the reproduced URLs asserting none reaches TIER_PRIMARY and Reuters outranks them.

entries.title: On the keyless search tier (no Docker/SearXNG, the default for most users) chat web_search times out at its 25 s tool cap because DuckDuckGo, first in the fixed chain, burns ~41 s of nested retries before a healthy Brave (0.9 s) is tried; the model then blames the network and suggests 'a lighter depth'
entries.repro: Sidecar booted without Docker (/search/status t1_keyless, all engines 'available'); vy.py invoke copilot 'Use your web_search tool to find recent news about Dixon Technologies and cite the sources' --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b -> tool timeout; model: 'there was a timeout error ... try again ... at a lighter depth' (2/2 runs). Direct handler timing: ddg FAIL 20.5 s, ddg FAIL 20.4 s, brave ok 0.9 s -> 42.5 s total.
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/failure-inducer/44-keyless-engine-timing.txt, 42-websearch-direct.txt, 41-deadsearxng-nodocker-websearch.txt, 43-nodocker-websearch-2nd.txt, 40-nodocker-status.txt; sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:313 (25 s), catalog.py:1572 (research-domain timeout hint), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:652-666 (wait_for), sidecar/services/search/keyless.py:53 (fixed ddg->brave->mojeek), keyless.py:150-190, keyless.py:201-232, sidecar/services/search/pacing.py:42 (2 attempts/engine), sidecar/services/search/ddg.py:60 (2 inner attempts), ddg.py:84 (12 s timeout). Refuters: SURF admitted high; COD-6 admitted_with_correction medium (outer 25 s bound exists, but DDG's nested budget exceeds it so failover never happens) - the live repro makes that corrected mechanism a core-flow failure, high kept.
entries.root_cause: Three independently reasonable retry layers (keyless 2 attempts x ddg 2 attempts x 12 s timeouts) with no per-engine deadline exceed the 25 s outer tool cap, so wait_for cancels before rotation reaches the next engine; the timeout hint is the research tool's copy.
entries.fix_shape: Give keyless.search a per-engine deadline that fits inside the tool cap (e.g. 6 s, no second attempt after a transport timeout), drop ddg.py's private retry loop now that keyless owns retry, and give web_search its own timeout hint naming the search tier. Pin with a test where the ddg stub hangs and brave answers, asserting web_search returns brave rows inside the catalog timeout.

entries.title: DEEP/ULTRA research never meters tokens or spend: the BudgetGuard has no token/spend ceiling, every loop site records usage=None, and the brief header shows no cost although dozens of paid LLM calls were billed
entries.repro: Run any DEEP brief on an OpenRouter paid model: deep_research._run_native builds BudgetGuard(max_steps=..., max_wall_seconds=...) only; oneshot.complete returns bare str; every loop site calls budget.record(None, model, provider) -> brief.cost carries zero tokens/spend and BriefPanel omits the segments.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:232-236, deep_research.py:322-325; sidecar/services/research/iter.py:585, iter.py:962, iter.py:1023, iter.py:1146; sidecar/services/research/deep.py:19-25, deep.py:1214; sidecar/services/research/verify.py:319; sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:95-107, budget_guard.py:116; src/modules/research/BriefPanel.tsx:113-146; spec FR-072/074/075. Refuter: admitted, high. Cross-cluster: same defect as R15-AGENT-012 (COD-research-extraction-synthesis-2, agent cluster) - the lead should fold the two at build time.
entries.root_cause: oneshot.complete drops the adapter's LLMUsage and returns text only, so research loops have nothing to record; the guard is built without the agent-invoke budget's token/spend ceilings.
entries.fix_shape: Make oneshot.complete return (text, usage), pass usage into budget.record at every research site, construct the research guard with the invoking run's token/spend ceilings so the existing breach path forces synthesis. Pin with a test that a stubbed-usage DEEP run reports non-zero brief.cost and breaches on a tiny max_spend_usd.

entries.title: Settings certifies any string as a working OpenRouter key ('research bills to it'), and when hosted Tier B research then 401s the trace shows only ok steps and 'done' - the failure reaches only the model, which answers with unfetched 'sources'
entries.repro: Settings -> AI Providers -> OpenRouter -> paste 'sk-or-v1-R15CANARY-this-is-not-a-real-key' -> POST /llm/keys/validate {ok:true}; Tier B card: 'OpenRouter key configured - research bills to it.' Then Tier B research with that key (vy.py invoke copilot ... --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --tier tier_b): stream = 2 research_step frames both 'ok', then 'done'; no error step/frame; llama3.1:8b answered with 'Brief sources: Wikipedia, Forbes, Bloomberg' (none fetched).
entries.evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/10-settings-panel-replay.json (S2), G01-tierb-fake-openrouter-key.jsonl + .stdout.txt, http-log.jsonl B01/B12; sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:842-849 (validate = models.list()), sidecar/services/llm/openrouter_catalog.py:15 (/api/v1/models is unauthenticated), sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:682, deep_research.py:723-724 (HTTP error returns ok:false without a _step), src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:1103-1105. Refuter: admitted_with_correction, high (model did disclose it could not fetch; no brief was published; fabrication is the chat-text source list). Validation half's code root cause is R15-CODE-AGENT-003 (COD-llm-adapters-2-4, code-agent cluster).
entries.root_cause: OpenRouter key validation calls a public endpoint, so it cannot fail on a bad key; run_research_model_brief returns ok:false on HTTPStatusError without emitting an error step, so the trace and panel never show the failure.
entries.fix_shape: Validate OpenRouter against an authenticated endpoint (GET /api/v1/auth/key with the key; 401 -> invalid); in run_research_model_brief emit _step('error', <humanised 401 message>) before returning ok:false. Pin with a test that a 401 from the hosted research call produces an error research_step on the stream.

entries.title: A BSE-XBRL institutional-holding figure is shown in the brief labelled 'NSE shareholding filing, <NSE quarter>' - the service's honest split_source/split_as_of stamp is discarded one layer up
entries.repro: Dual-listed Indian name whose latest NSE quarterly master row has no matching BSE XBRL quarter (nearest-quarter branch, corporate_disclosures.py:530): _merge_bse_split stamps split_source='BSE', split_as_of=<BSE quarter>; ownership_check._fetch_latest copies institutions_percent but sets as_of_quarter=latest.quarter_end and source=latest.source (NSE) -> semantics renders basis 'NSE shareholding filing, <NSE quarter>' on institutions_percent_exchange.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:507, corporate_disclosures.py:538, sidecar/services/ownership_check.py:126-132, sidecar/services/research/semantics.py:555, semantics.py:559, semantics.py:578, sidecar/models/announcements.py:133. Refuter: admitted_with_correction critical -> high (live RELIANCE/SIL/TCS have split_as_of == quarter_end, so the wrong-QUARTER label fires only in the nearest-quarter branch; the 'NSE' source label on a BSE figure is always-on; both exchanges carry the same SEBI SHP filing).
entries.root_cause: split_source/split_as_of have no production reader; _fetch_latest re-derives provenance from the NSE master row.
entries.fix_shape: In _fetch_latest set as_of_quarter=(latest.split_as_of or latest.quarter_end).isoformat() and carry latest.split_source into source when the institutions figure was merged. Pin with a test where the merged BSE quarter differs from the NSE master quarter and the rendered basis names BSE and the BSE quarter.

entries.title: The research structured filings floor is the 5 newest attachments, not the results filing first: gather_floor omits the sub_question that turns on results-banding, so in results season thin-web runs cite procedural intimations
entries.repro: Thin-web DEEP run on an Indian listing in results season: gather_floor (disclosures.py:169) calls announcement_rows without sub_question -> results_shaped False -> no sort -> the floor's 5 citable rows are the 5 newest attachments (procedural intimations), while gather (:324) passes sub_question and ranks the outcome filing first.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/research/disclosures.py:169, disclosures.py:222, disclosures.py:252, disclosures.py:324, sidecar/services/research/iter.py:351, iter.py:924, deep.py:731-738 (refuter mitigation). Refuter: admitted_with_correction high -> medium (per-researcher gather still ranks results filings whenever a results-shaped researcher fires).
entries.root_cause: Results-banding is conditional on a sub_question that the floor path never supplies.
entries.fix_shape: Pass sub_question='results' from gather_floor (or make banding unconditional when sub_question is empty). Pin with a test feeding 6 announcements (5 procedural newer, 1 results older) through gather_floor and asserting the results filing is row 1.

entries.title: FAST research's filings leg always stamps provider 'nse+bse', including BSE-only listings and single-lane outages, overriding the sources/errors the announcements tool already reports
entries.repro: BSE lane down (AnnouncementsResponse.errors set, sources == ['NSE']) or any BSE-only small-cap -> research/fast._filings_leg sets value['provider']='nse+bse' whenever ok -> FR-041 provenance badge claims both exchanges served.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/research/fast.py:437, sidecar/models/announcements.py:52, announcements.py:56, sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:299. Refuter: admitted, medium (also every BSE-only listing, the thin small-cap class).
entries.root_cause: The consumer hardcodes the provider string instead of reading result.sources.
entries.fix_shape: value['provider'] = '+'.join(result.get('sources') or []) or 'exchange'. Pin with a test where the announcements stub returns sources=['BSE'] and the leg's provider is 'BSE'.

entries.title: A cut-off answer is shown as complete: the Anthropic adapter hard-caps every call at 4096 output tokens and no layer (oneshot, runtime, UI) acts on a max_tokens/length finish_reason, so a truncated deep-research synthesis renders as final
entries.repro: Deep-research synthesis or a long agent answer on Anthropic -> adapter sends max_tokens=4096 (no caller sets it) -> stream stops mid-sentence with stop_reason 'max_tokens' -> LLMDoneEvent.finish_reason='max_tokens' -> oneshot.complete returns the partial text; agent_runtime only inspects 'content_filter'; streaming.ts decodes finishReason with no consumer.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/llm/anthropic.py:36-37, anthropic.py:110, sidecar/services/llm/oneshot.py:84-92, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:102, agent_runtime.py:1483-1493, sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:323, src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:327-342. Refuter: admitted, medium. Cross-cluster: overlaps R15-AGENT-026 (COD-error-layer-2-3, SURF-FAILURE-INDUCER-1, agent cluster) on the chat side; this entry owns the research-synthesis path and the Anthropic cap.
entries.root_cause: DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS=4096 is the only value ever sent; finish_reason is carried end to end but never acted on.
entries.fix_shape: Raise the Anthropic default to the model's documented output ceiling from the registry; have oneshot.complete and the runtime flag finish_reason in {'max_tokens','length'} as a visible 'answer truncated' note on the brief/message. Pin with a stub adapter returning finish_reason='max_tokens' and assert the note is emitted.

entries.title: ULTRA's independence floor double-counts the native channel, so a claim resting on one domain reached by both lanes is rendered 'AGREE (corroborated across channels)' under a '2 independent sources' promise
entries.repro: Dual-channel ULTRA claim whose only evidence is one domain d reached by SearXNG and native: domains = {d}; independence = len(domains) + 1 (native_text) = 2 >= min_domains 2 -> verdict runs, AGREE renders 'AGREE (corroborated across channels)'.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/research/verify.py:250-255, verify.py:265-266, verify.py:365, verify.py:371-373, verify.py:391-393, sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:274. Refuter: admitted_with_correction high -> medium (figure is still sourced from one domain; overstates independence rather than publishing an unsourced number).
entries.root_cause: Line 365 already folds native citation domains into `domains`; line 373 adds +1 for the same lane.
entries.fix_shape: independence = len(domains) + (1 if native_text and not native_rows else 0); gate 'corroborated' on the two channels resting on different domains. Pin with a one-domain-both-lanes test asserting UNVERIFIED (insufficient independence).

entries.title: ULTRA never records the always-on exchange-filings floor rows as [n] citations (DEEP does): the pre-seeded snapshot trips the guard that also controls _record_web
entries.repro: ULTRA on a thin-web Indian micro-cap: run_heavy_research pre-seeds snapshot['disclosures'] (iter.py:918-929) -> each explorer's `structured.get('disclosures') is None` is False -> the block containing _record_web(floor['rows']) is skipped -> no floor citations and no web coverage credit for them; same query at DEEP records them.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/research/iter.py:350, iter.py:357-363, iter.py:918-929, sidecar/services/research/disclosures.py:127-137, deep.py:731-759 (refuter mitigation). Refuter: admitted_with_correction high -> medium (disclosure-shaped researchers still cite announcement rows; loss is the always-on floor citations and their coverage credit).
entries.root_cause: One guard controls two unrelated actions: fetching the floor and recording its rows as sources.
entries.fix_shape: Split the guard: pull only when absent, but always _record_web(structured['disclosures']['rows']) (once, in run_heavy_research). Pin with a test that an ULTRA run over a stub floor lists the floor rows in brief.sources.

entries.title: An exception inside ULTRA's run_heavy_research escapes _run_loop and loses the brief, while the identical failure at DEEP degrades to the single-pass fallback with an honest note
entries.repro: Any exception raised in run_heavy_research (resolve_target, snapshot_structured at iter.py:915, gather_floor, webweaver synthesis, citation integrity - all outside any guard) -> escapes _run_loop to agent_runtime._dispatch_tool -> 'tool research raised' to the model, no brief. At DEEP the same exception is caught at deep_research.py:283 and falls back.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:259-280, deep_research.py:281-296, sidecar/services/research/iter.py:915, sidecar/services/research/fast.py:377-385. Refuter: admitted_with_correction high -> medium (no concrete raising path demonstrated; runtime catches the escape). Related: R15-CODE-RESEARCH-002 (snapshot_structured's gather lacks return_exceptions).
entries.root_cause: The heavy branch of _run_loop was added without the try/except the iter branch has.
entries.fix_shape: Give the heavy branch the same try/except + fallback + note as the iter branch. Pin with a test that a raising run_heavy_research stub still yields a published single-pass brief with the fallback note.

entries.title: DEEP/ULTRA researchers query SEC EDGAR for Indian listings on any filing/sec/insider-shaped sub-question (and on 'sector'/'second' via a bare 'sec' substring), showing the model an empty-success SEC list or a false 'feed outage' framing
entries.repro: DEEP/ULTRA on an NSE/BSE name with a filing-shaped sub-question: deep.py:707-709 picks sec_filings_list with the Indian symbol; with sec-edgar-mcp up /sec/filings?symbol=RELIANCE.NS returns filings:[] wrapped ok:true (reads as 'no filings'); with it down deep.py:806-812 injects 'temporarily unavailable ... NOT evidence the data does not exist'. fast._filings_leg routes the same decision by region to corporate_announcements.

entries.title: A 200-status CAPTCHA/block page from a keyless engine is recorded as a healthy empty answer and resets that engine's circuit breaker, so a blocking engine is never benched and an all-blocked search reports 'found nothing' instead of 'rate-limited'
entries.repro: KeylessSearchBackend(engines={'ddg': stub}) where stub returns one row 'Unusual traffic from your computer network' / 'verify you are a human' -> SearchResponse(results=[], backend='keyless') ok, breaker_for('ddg').state=='closed', _failures==0. entries.evidence: sidecar/services/search/keyless.py:75, keyless.py:163-165, keyless.py:175-176, keyless.py:186, keyless.py:194, sidecar/services/search/ddg.py:385-394, sidecar/services/agent_tools/web_search.py:157.
